base.description: Roles and permissions are global to the deployment. The default.

workspaces.description: Users belong to workspaces and hold different roles in each. Workspace-scoped requests carry an X-Workspace-Id header.

postInstall: Set DATABASE_URL in .env (see .env.example)

Set AUTH_JWT_SECRET in .env — a base64-encoded 256-bit (or longer) secret, e.g.: openssl rand -base64 32. The app refuses to start without it; there is no default and nothing is generated for you. Changing it invalidates every outstanding token.

package.json, tsconfig.json, nest-cli.json (NestJS combos only), tsconfig.build.json, .prettierrc, .prettierignore, eslint.config.mjs, commitlint.config.ts, and docker-compose.yml are installed at the project root — if you already had any of these, they are overwritten (not merged) with this combo's version. Review the diff before committing; re-add your own customizations afterward. tsconfig.json already sets module/moduleResolution for this registry's CommonJS build and the @/core/*, @/database/* path aliases — no manual edits needed.
Run: npx prisma generate
Run: npx prisma migrate deploy

Seed RBAC: run npm run seed (already wired into the installed package.json) — it is idempotent, and seeds the permission catalog and the default admin/member roles. Nothing is authorized until it has run at least once.
Optional: set SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL and SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD before seeding to also create an initial admin user. Without them the seeder skips the admin rather than inventing a password.

Assemble your own app.module.ts: import ConfigModule.forRoot(), ThrottlerModule.forRoot([...]), CoreAuthModule.forRoot({...}), and the 5 feature modules (AuthModule, AdminModule, RoleModule, PermissionModule, AuditLogModule); register APP_GUARD ThrottlerGuard, APP_FILTER AuthCoreErrorFilter, and APP_INTERCEPTOR ResponseInterceptor as providers — see examples/nestjs-prisma-app/src/app.module.ts for a working example. CoreAuthModule.forRoot() is the only piece that still takes config (AUTH_CONFIG overrides, cache/rate-limit stores, OAuth credentials); everything else is ordinary application wiring, not something this library assembles for you.

Every route is versioned under v1 in its own controller path (e.g. AuthController is @Controller("v1/auth")) — set the deployment-level "api" segment yourself in main.ts: app.setGlobalPrefix("api", { exclude: ["/", "health"] }) (adjust the exclude list to your own app's public routes), giving /api/v1/auth/..., /api/v1/admin/..., /api/v1/roles, /api/v1/permissions, /api/v1/audit-log. Docs/Swagger middleware is unaffected either way, since setGlobalPrefix only touches Nest-routed controllers, not raw app.use() middleware.

Optional: wire SwaggerModule.setup('docs', app, document) in your main.ts to serve the OpenAPI spec this combo's controller is already decorated for — see examples/nestjs-prisma-app/src/main.ts for a working example

Run: npm install, then npm run start:dev for a real nest start --watch dev loop (or npm run build && npm run start:prod for a production build) — package.json already has build/start/start:dev/lint/format scripts wired up. main.ts/app.module.ts/app.controller.ts/app.service.ts still are not provided and need to be assembled by hand per the steps above.

Logging: requests and the permissionCacheStore/rateLimitStore warning are written to ./logs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<debug|info|warn|error>/<auth|admin|roles|permissions|audit-log>.log, plus a combined ./logs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<debug|info|warn|error>.log per level (line-delimited JSON, prod-standard shape: string level, ISO-8601 time) for a log shipper (e.g. Filebeat) to tail — point its paths glob at logs/*/info.log, logs/*/warn.log, logs/*/error.log (and logs/*/debug.log if you want request-start noise too), not the per-module subfolders, or every line is double-ingested. Every line belonging to one request carries the same traceId (including calls made deep inside a service that never sees req/res, via AsyncLocalStorage) plus a nested payload/response (request/response body, with password/token/secret/otp/etc. fields redacted); the "end" line also carries startedAt + durationMs. LOG_DIR overrides the base directory (default ./logs). Nothing here ever deletes an old log file — retention/cleanup is a manual ops decision (cron, logrotate, your shipper's own policy), not something this library automates. Register APP_INTERCEPTOR RequestLoggerInterceptor *before* ResponseInterceptor (Nest's first-registered interceptor is outermost, so it sees the already-enveloped response body) in your app.module.ts to enable request logging — see examples/nestjs-prisma-app/src/app.module.ts.

postInstall: Copy .env.example to .env and set VITE_AUTH_API_URL to your running simple-auth-kit backend's URL
Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory

If this isn't already a git repository, run: git init — husky's pre-commit/commit-msg hooks (wired via the "prepare": "husky" script) only activate once a .git directory exists; without one, npm install's prepare step no-ops harmlessly
Run: npm run dev — starts the Vite dev server

workspaces: Pair with a workspaces-variant backend (e.g. nestjs-prisma --workspaces) — this console sends X-Workspace-Id on every workspace-scoped request

postInstall: Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory

Set EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL if your backend isn't at http://localhost:3001 — on an Android emulator that's http://10.0.2.2:3001, not localhost
Run: npm start — opens the Expo dev tools (android/ios/web from there)

Set the backend URL your platform actually needs — see src/api/authClient.ts (Android emulator: 10.0.2.2, not localhost)

postInstall: Copy .env.example to .env and set NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL to your running simple-auth-kit backend's URL
Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory

If this isn't already a git repository, run: git init — husky's pre-commit/commit-msg hooks (wired via the "prepare": "husky" script) only activate once a .git directory exists; without one, npm install's prepare step no-ops harmlessly
Run: npm run dev — starts the Next.js dev server on port 3000

Note: base and workspaces variants deliberately use different route-guarding trust models — base uses NextAuth edge middleware (src/proxy.ts), workspaces uses a client-side session recheck on every navigation. Both are correct for their own architecture; see registry/admin-apps/README.md for why they aren't unified.

base: Also set AUTH_SECRET in .env — the NextAuth v5 session-JWT signing secret. Generate one with: npx auth secret (or: openssl rand -base64 32)
